C-73.Name: Systematic regression baseline: affordance audit and release-checklist revival
C-73.Summary: Stop waiting for users to find trivially discoverable defects. Three layers: a source-level audit that every advertised chord (registry palette arrays, native menu accelerators, front-menu hints) has a real dispatch route; a behavioral e2e audit that pressed chords, every registry leaf dispatched through the menu bridge, and welcome action buttons produce an observable response; and the manual regression checklist rewritten for the 2.5.x surface and bound to train-freeze execution.
C-73.ApprovalBasis: Owner asked on 2026-10-20 for a systematic regression pass instead of waiting for users to catch childish bugs, and approved the three-layer proposal with «поехали».
C-73.ProblemEvidence: The 2026-10-19/20 waves: FIX-005 and FIX-006 (advertised ⇧⌘P/⇧⌘N/⌘1–6 chords with no dispatch route), FIX-009 (dead Last-session button), FIX-010 (⇧⌘P reserved yet UC-025 unrouted) — four of ten defects in the "advertised affordance does nothing" class that any breadth pass catches, while all existing coverage is per-defect and reactive. The manual checklist tests/regression-tests.json was last executed 2026-05-21 on v2.0.0-alpha.7 with ~80% items pending.

Goals.Goal: Any chord shown to the user (palette, native menu, front menu) must have a dispatch route, and any reserved chord must stay unclaimed — enforced in CI.
Any registry command reachable from the native menu must respond when dispatched, with new bridge warnings failing the gate.
Welcome-screen action buttons must fire their action; the known-dead FIX-009 case stays visible as fixme until repaired.
The human regression checklist matches the 2.5.x feature surface and runs before every train candidate freeze.

Constraints.Constraint: Test-only and documentation change: no runtime behavior changes except none; FIX-012 found by the audit is recorded, not repaired here.
CI must stay green: known-open findings (help.rate capability gating, FIX-012 walk warning) enter documented allowlists referencing their trackers, never silent skips.
Extraction-based tests follow the house menu-consistency pattern: source-scan with population guards that fail loudly on extractor drift rather than passing vacuously.
English-only artifacts; GRACE verification projections updated in the same change.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No repair of FIX-009, FIX-011, FIX-012 or any open defect — the audit records them.
No new runtime features, no Command Palette (UC-025) implementation; ⇧⌘P stays reserved.
No mobile, MAS or site surfaces; desktop renderer harness only.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: tests/renderer/commands/shortcut-routing-audit.test.js passes with seven assertions: advertised↔routed both directions, front-menu parity, collision detection, registry/native agreement per shared id, and reservation of Meta+Shift+P; population guards fail on empty extraction.

tests/e2e/affordance-audit.spec.ts passes in Chromium: real-key chord responses with markdown-anchored duplicate/heading cases, the menu-bridge walk over ≥40 registry leaves with a reasoned allowlist and zero unexpected bridge warnings, welcome action responses, and the FIX-009 fixme case present.

tests/regression-tests.json describes the 2.5.x surface (welcome, tabs ownership, split view, diff, lock, viewer, pele, localization) with an executionProtocol binding full passes to train-freeze and targeted passes to repairs.
Verification projections updated: V-M-009 scenario-17, V-M-012 scenario-71, index comments; grace lint passes on current assertions.

AffectedAreas.Area: tests/renderer/commands/ (new audit beside menu-consistency and paragraph-shortcuts), tests/e2e/ (new affordance-audit spec), tests/regression-tests.json, .grace/verification/runtime.xml + index.xml, docs/release-trains/2.5.x-next.md (FIX-012 record).
